name: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius and the burial of Pompeii
date_range: AD 79 (day and month disputed), about 18-19 hours of pumice fall, surges the next morning
location: Pompeii, Bay of Naples, Roman Italy
tone_note: Comic tier for Tony's slapstick and the absurd details. The victims are never the joke: their deaths are stated plainly, never shown, never mocked.

chronology.beat: Ordinary town life, tremors ignored, then just after midday the eruption begins and white pumice starts to fall
The afternoon: pumice piles up, roofs start to give way
Leave or stay: most people leave; the sea route in the bay is blocked
Night: darkness and fear of the gods (documented at Misenum and Stabiae)
Early morning: the surges reach Pompeii
Aftermath: the city lies under metres of pumice and ash
What really happened, and the open questions (the date)

chronology_note: Days 4-7 are thin. Before a real week is produced, the fact-checker should research a run-up (life in Pompeii before) and the aftermath.

facts.text: The eruption happened in the year AD 79.
facts.source: Sigurdsson et al. 1985 (abstract); Luongo et al. 2003 (abstract)

facts.text: The month and day are debated: manuscripts of Pliny give 24 August, while autumn fruit, heavy clothing, sealed wine jars and a charcoal inscription dated 17 October (year unknown) point to the autumn.
facts.source: Wikipedia: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD; archaeology.org 2018

facts.text: The main eruption began shortly after noon, about 1 pm, after a small opening explosion.
facts.source: Sigurdsson 1985; Pliny the Younger, Letters 6.16 (seventh hour); Tulane lecture page

facts.text: Pliny the Younger compared the eruption cloud to an umbrella pine: a tall trunk that spread out into branches at the top.
The column rose about 15 to 30 km high, many miles into the sky.
facts.source: Wikipedia: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD; Harvard exhibition page

facts.text: White pumice began falling on Pompeii at about 1 pm, about the same time the column rose.
facts.source: Sparice et al. 2024; Tulane lecture page; Sigurdsson 1985

facts.text: White pumice fell for about 7 hours, then grey pumice; the whole fall lasted about 18 to 19 hours.
The pumice piled up at about 15 cm per hour.
The white pumice pieces were up to about 3 cm across, light, coarse and angular.
facts.source: Wikipedia: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD; Sparice 2024; Pliny 6.16 (light stones)

facts.text: Most roofs in Pompeii collapsed a few hours into the pumice fall, under about 40 to 60 cm of pumice; some sloped roofs shed it and held.
394 victims were found in the pumice-fall layer; most died when roofs and walls collapsed on them.
650 victims were found in the surge deposits of the next morning, about half on the roads and half in buildings.
About 1,150 victims have been found at Pompeii in total.
Most of Pompeii's inhabitants left the city during the first phase, while the pumice was falling.
facts.source: Luongo et al. 2003 (abstract); Western Australian Museum

facts.text: The first surge reached Pompeii early in the morning of the next day, around 7 am (sources range from about 6:30 to 8).
Small earthquakes in the days before were common in the region and were not taken as a warning.
facts.source: Wikipedia: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD; Pliny 6.20

facts.text: At Stabiae, Pliny the Elder's party tied pillows to their heads with cloths to protect themselves from the falling stones (that night).
Pompeii lies about 8 km from Vesuvius.
Pompeii's streets were paved with lava stone, had raised pavements, and about 316 big stepping stones so people could cross dirty or wet streets; the gaps let cart wheels pass between them.
facts.source: AJA review of Poehler, The Traffic Systems of Pompeii; AJA abstract of Poehler and Crowther, Paving Pompeii

facts.text: Carbonized round loaves about 20 cm across were found, scored into 6 to 8 wedges, some stamped with the baker's name; 81 loaves were found in one oven.
Pompeii's bakeries ground grain in big lava-stone mills, often four of them, turned by donkeys.
During the eruption, some people raised their hands to the gods, others said there were no gods left and that this was the world's last, eternal night (Pliny, at Misenum).
Some ancient writers saw that Vesuvius looked volcanic (Strabo compared it with Etna), but nobody treated it as a danger.
Pompeii had more than 30 bakeries (counts vary between 31 and about 40).
At Stabiae the sea was too rough and the shore blocked by debris, so Pliny the Elder's rescue by ship could not get away.
Pompeii ended up buried under about 2.8 m of pumice and ash.
facts.source: Wikipedia: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD
